la:noun:Rhodanus.html:
Rhŏdănus, i, m.
The Rhone, a river in Gaul, ; ; ; Varr. ap. ; ; Planc. ap. ; ; ; : Rhodani potor,a dweller by the Rhone, et saep.—Hence,
RHODANICI NAVTAE, sailors or boatmen on the Rhone, ; ; in sing., . —
Rhŏdănītis, ĭdis, f.adj., of or belonging to the Rhone: urbes,situated upon the Rhone,—
Rhŏdănū-sĭa, ae, f., the Rhone City, Lugdunum, now Lyons, —
Meton., the dwellers by the Rhone, the Gauls: Rheno Rhodanoque subactis,.

la:adj:rhetoricus.html:
rhētŏrĭcus, a, um, adj., = ῥητορικός,
of or belonging to a rhetorician, rhetorical.
Adj.: nostro more aliquando, non rhetorico loquamur,: ars,i. e. a treatise on rhetoric,: rhetorici doctores,i. e. teachers of rhetoric,: syllogismus,; : libri,books on rhetoric,. — Hence,
Substt.
rhētŏrĭca, ae, or rhētŏrĭcē, ēs, f. (the first form in Cic., the latter in Quint.), the art of oratory, rhetoric: dicam, si potero, rhetorice, sed hac rhetoricā philosophorum, non nostrā illa forensi,: rhetorice est bene dicendi scientia,: et rhetorice, cui nomen vis eloquentiae dedit,: jus rhetorices, id. prooem. § 23: rhetoricen exercere,; : de rhetorice,. —
rhētŏrĭci, ōrum, m.
Teachers of oratory, = rhetores, ipsi magistri, qui rhetorici vocantur, .—
Books on rhetoric: nisi rhetoricos suos (the erroneouslynamed books de Inventione) ipse adulescenti sibi elapsos diceret (Cicero),; so, in rhetoricis,; also in sing.: sicut ex Ciceronis rhetorico primo manifestum est,; .—
Neutr. plur.: rhētŏrĭca, ōrum, rhetoric: rhetorica mihi vestra sunt nota,.— Adv.: rhētŏrĭcē, in an oratorical or rhetorical manner, oratorically, rhetorically: rhetorice igitur nos mavis quam dialectice disputare?: ejus mortem rhetorice et tragice ornare,: quam rhetorice!.

la:noun:rhetor.html:
rhētor, ŏris, m., = ῥήτωρ,
a teacher of oratory or rhetoric, a rhetorician: eos, qui rhetores nominarentur et qui dicendi praecepta traderent, nihil plane tenere,; cf. : in rhetorum

scholis, ; : rhetorum artes,: rhetorum epilogus,; : (pueri) priusquam tradantur rhetori,; ; and 35; .— *

After the Greek manner, an orator; but with contempt, a rhetorician, speechifier, etc.: stultitia rhetoris Attica,; cf. with § 1.
